answer: Admission needs a cross-cluster quorum: attesters from separate branches of the trust graph each sign a juniper for the newcomer and lock 1 nectar, forfeited if the seat is proven a clone. The summit records every juniper and counts k, the seats already admitted that share any signer with the newcomer. The newcomer then needs junipers from 3+k branches with no common ancestor. An honest arrival buys 3 signatures. An operator reusing bribed signers for 100 clones needs 5,250, or must bribe 300 unrelated attesters, each risking its own nectar.
